Operating evidence for incomplete repeated-subject time courses. The Synthetic repeated-subject
time course experiment to assess the declared condition target contrasts CM with CTL. (A)
Target loading recovery at the disclosed absolute cosine threshold. (B) Mean absolute loading
cosine for the planted target under condition-stratified complete-subject bootstrap. (C)
Estimability of the adjusted condition-by-time random-intercept-plus-slope model after target
recovery. Red circles are estimated values; panels A and C show outer-replicate probabilities
and panel B shows mean cosine; crosses mark a scientific quantity that was not estimable and
are positioned near zero without encoding a probability; hollow triangles at the left margin
independently mark incomplete outer execution or target-axis refitting; finite values still
summarize all completed refits. The analysis unit is one repeatedly observed synthetic mouse;
the design is four CTL and four CM mice intended at each of four observed times; mouse
identity, condition, and time remain explicit; the estimand is standardized condition-by-time
interaction; time is recorded as weeks (times 0, 1, 2, 3) in synthetic study units; adjustment
uses batch. 5 deterministic outer replicates and 5 complete-subject target-axis bootstrap
refits per replicate were requested; 19 of 20 outer executions and 95 of 100 target-axis refits
completed. No visit is imputed or treated as an independent animal. Complete trajectories
removes no observations; One internal visit missing removes cm1 at time 2; One mouse drops out
removes cm1 at time 2, cm1 at time 3; Two disease mice drop out removes cm1 at time 2, cm1 at
time 3, cm2 at time 2, cm2 at time 3. Recovery uses an absolute loading-cosine threshold of
0.90. This is disclosed synthetic calibration evidence, not an acceptance result or universal
sample-size rule.
